da-false-claim.evidence: atom-knot-unique.md:14-29 'Proof': asserts two braids realising the same NF 'differ only by a sequence of' R-II/R-III/far-commutations, 'Each is a categorical Markov move, so the closures are isotopic.' But sameness of NF (a Hecke-algebra normal form) does NOT imply the two BRAIDS are related by Reidemeister/Markov moves — distinct braids can share a Hecke NF yet have non-isotopic closures (the Hecke quotient collapses braid information). The Scope section (md:31-39) even concedes 'different w_q^Z realisations ... yield different isotopy classes'.
da-false-claim.notes: The proof conflates equality in H_n(q) (NF) with isotopy of Markov closures. NF equality is necessary, not sufficient, for closure isotopy. The proof step 'differ only by R-II/R-III/far commutations' is unjustified — that is the Markov theorem's content, not a consequence of NF equality. Borderline false-as-proved; flag warn pending the missing Markov-move lemma.

da-vacuous.evidence: atom-knot-unique.lean:17-26: theorem AtomKnot.unique_up_to_markov takes h_Z,h_N,h_proton,h_neutron,h_inter (ALL five record fields equal) and concludes K₁=K₂ via 'cases K₁; cases K₂; congr <;> assumption'. This is the trivial fact that a structure is determined by its fields — a tautology with no Markov/isotopy/Hecke content whatsoever.
da-vacuous.notes: The Lean 'proof' is vacuous: it proves record extensionality, not 'unique up to Markov equivalence'. The hypotheses already assume everything (all fields equal ⇒ records equal). Self-assuming projection in the §1a sense.

da-circular.notes: Not back-fitting a numerical target; the issue is vacuity/divergence, not circular calibration.

da-overclaim.evidence: atom-knot-unique.ts:1 kind=proposition titled 'Uniqueness of the atom-knot up to Markov equivalence', .md states closures are isotopic (md:8-12). The actual Lean (lean:17-26) proves only record equality from all-fields-equal — strictly weaker than 'closures isotopic'. The narrative proof's Markov-move step is asserted, not derived (md:16-28).
da-overclaim.notes: The proposition claims a topological uniqueness (isotopy of S^3 closures) that neither the narrative proof (asserted Markov-move reduction) nor the Lean (trivial record extensionality) establishes. Conditional/assumed-as-proved.

da-non-sequitur.evidence: atom-knot-unique.md:16-28: 'Two braids realising the same NF differ only by a sequence of [R-II / R-III / far commutations] ... Each is a categorical Markov move, so the closures are isotopic.' The 'so' does not follow: equality of Hecke normal forms does not entail the braids are connected by Reidemeister/Markov moves (the Hecke quotient is many-to-one on braids). The required lemma — 'same NF ⇒ Markov-equivalent braids' — is missing and is in fact false in general.
da-non-sequitur.notes: This is the load-bearing inferential gap. NF equality lives in the algebra H_n(q); braid/closure isotopy lives in B_n/S^3. The map is not injective, so the implication is a non-sequitur.

da-lean-narrative-divergence.evidence: atom-knot-unique.md claims 'Markov closures are isotopic in S^3' (md:8-12) under shared NF. atom-knot-unique.lean:17-26 instead proves K₁=K₂ (strict record equality) from ALL five fields being equal, by 'congr <;> assumption' — a different and strictly weaker statement that mentions neither Markov closure nor isotopy. Additionally, .ts:6 lean.ref='qou:QOU.BraidKnot.AtomKnot.unique' but the actual decl is 'AtomKnot.unique_up_to_markov' (lean:17) — the ref name does not resolve to the declaration.
da-lean-narrative-divergence.notes: Twofold divergence: (1) Lean proves record extensionality, not Markov-isotopy uniqueness — proof-statement-integrity failure; (2) ref/decl name mismatch (unique vs unique_up_to_markov). The Lean is vacuously implied and does not capture the .md claim.

da-citation-misuse.evidence: atom-knot-unique.lean:16 '-- Ref: [manuscript] thm:jones-markov-trace' attaches the Jones–Markov-trace manuscript reference to a theorem (record extensionality) that uses none of that content. The .md (md:27-29) likewise cites thm:jones-markov-trace to justify 'Each is a categorical Markov move', but that theorem gives the trace, not the Markov-move-equivalence of NF-equal braids.
da-citation-misuse.notes: The cited result (Jones–Markov trace) is invoked to license the Markov-move reduction, which it does not supply (Markov's theorem on braid equivalence is the relevant result, not the trace). Mild misattribution.

da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: atom-knot-unique.md:2-3 'unique up to Markov equivalence' vs md:8 'isotopic in S^3' vs md:32 'up to isotopy, not up to NF strict equality' — three notions (Markov equivalence of braids, isotopy of closures, NF equality) are used somewhat interchangeably. The Lean adds a fourth (record equality). 'The atom-knot of type (Z,N)' presupposes a canonical representative whose uniqueness is exactly what's at issue.
da-definitional-ambiguity.notes: 'Unique' is overloaded across braid-Markov-equivalence, closure-isotopy, NF-equality, and record-equality; the block does not cleanly fix which uniqueness is claimed vs proved.

da-physical-implausibility.notes: The physical reading (isomers as distinct atom-knots at same (Z,N); md:37-39) is sensible. No units/conservation issue.

da-reproducibility.notes: No backing compute to be stale.

da-referee-verdict.evidence: verdict=major-revision. Strongest objection: the proposition claims Markov-equivalence/isotopy uniqueness, but (a) the narrative proof's central step 'same NF ⇒ braids related by Reidemeister/Markov moves' (md:16-28) is a non-sequitur (the Hecke quotient is many-to-one), and (b) the Lean (lean:17-26) proves only trivial record extensionality K₁=K₂ from all-fields-equal, not the topological claim — plus the .ts ref name (AtomKnot.unique) doesn't match the decl (AtomKnot.unique_up_to_markov).
da-referee-verdict.notes: referee_argument: As stated, the result is not established. Either prove the genuine lemma 'two braids with the same Hecke NF have Markov-equivalent closures' (which needs justification beyond NF equality and may require additional hypotheses, as the Scope section itself signals with the w_q^Z caveat), or restate the proposition as 'the NF block decomposition is unique' (the Diamond-Lemma fact that IS true) and drop the isotopy claim. Replace the vacuous Lean record-extensionality theorem with one that actually carries Markov-closure content, and fix the lean.ref name mismatch.
